title: Daily 02:30 across the US spring-forward gap

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.quote: Recurrence instances falling on invalid dates and times are ignored and not counted

normative.title: RFC 5545 erratum 4271 (Verified, Technical, §3.3.10 nonexistent local times)
normative.quote: invalid dates keep MUST-ignore; nonexistent local times are 'handled as specified in Section 3.3.5'

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.5 (DATE-TIME)
normative.quote: If the local time described does not occur ... the DATE-TIME value is interpreted using the UTC offset before the gap.

cases.label: drop
cases.note: Published RFC text: the nonexistent instance is ignored and not counted, so COUNT=4 reaches 2026-03-10.

cases.label: pre-gap-offset
cases.note: Erratum 4271 routed through §3.3.5: 02:30 EST = 07:30Z, which is 03:30 EDT in wall-clock terms.

expect.note: python-dateutil emits 2026-03-08T02:30:00-04:00, a datetime for which dateutil.tz.datetime_exists() returns False: it neither drops the instance nor resolves it via the pre-gap offset.

pandas@tz2026a.error: ValueError: 2026-03-08 02:30:00 is a nonexistent time due to daylight savings time. Try using the 'nonexistent' argument.

pandas@tz2026c.error: ValueError: 2026-03-08 02:30:00 is a nonexistent time due to daylight savings time. Try using the 'nonexistent' argument.

rationale: Three positions on nonexistent local times — published RFC, Verified erratum, and the most-used reference implementation — and none is what a user would predict. This is the vector that most directly falsifies 'RFC 5545 compliant' as a claim.

title: Daily 01:30 across the US autumn fold

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.5 (DATE-TIME)
normative.quote: If the local time described occurs more than once ... the DATE-TIME value refers to the first occurrence.

normative.title: RFC 5545 erratum 4271 (Verified, Technical, §3.3.10 nonexistent local times)

expect.note: The fold case IS settled by §3.3.5: first occurrence, i.e. the pre-transition offset. Emitting both instants, or only the second, is a conformance failure.

pandas@tz2026a.error: ValueError: Cannot infer dst time from 2026-11-01 01:30:00, try using the 'ambiguous' argument

pandas@tz2026c.error: ValueError: Cannot infer dst time from 2026-11-01 01:30:00, try using the 'ambiguous' argument

rationale: Deliberately classified NORMATIVE while its gap counterpart is AMBIGUOUS_STANDARD: §3.3.5 resolves the fold and leaves the gap to erratum 4271. Engines usually get the fold right and the gap wrong, and the asymmetry is only visible when the two are tested as a pair.

title: A recurrence whose local time is stable but whose UTC offset changes (the DST-safe property)

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.5 (DATE-TIME)
normative.note: a DATE-TIME with a TZID is a local time; the UTC instant is derived, not stored

expect.note: 09:00 local on all three dates; the UTC instants are 14:00Z, 13:00Z, 13:00Z. An engine that expands in UTC and converts back produces 08:00 or 10:00 local after the transition.

rationale: The defining property of zoned recurrence, and the one most often broken by engines that normalise to UTC on parse. Cheap to test, decisive, and the reason the corpus's output encoding carries both local and UTC forms.

title: Weekly 02:15 in Lord Howe (30-minute transition)

normative.title: RFC 5545 erratum 4271 (Verified, Technical, §3.3.10 nonexistent local times)

expect.note: Recorded, not scored. 2026-10-04T02:15 does not exist in Lord Howe (the gap is 02:00-02:30). Engines that resolve a gap by adding one hour land at 03:15, which is 45 minutes later than the pre-gap-offset answer of 02:30.

pandas@tz2026a.error: ValueError: 2026-10-04 02:15:00 is a nonexistent time due to daylight savings time. Try using the 'nonexistent' argument.

pandas@tz2026c.error: ValueError: 2026-10-04 02:15:00 is a nonexistent time due to daylight savings time. Try using the 'nonexistent' argument.

rationale: The half-hour transition is where a hard-coded one-hour correction becomes visibly wrong rather than merely arbitrary.

title: Daily 01:30 in Antarctica/Troll (two-hour transition)

normative.title: RFC 5545 erratum 4271 (Verified, Technical, §3.3.10 nonexistent local times)

expect.note: Recorded, not scored. Troll's 2026-03-29 transition is +00 to +02, so 01:30 and 02:30 both fail to exist. A one-hour correction lands inside the gap.

pandas@tz2026a.error: ValueError: 2026-03-29 01:30:00 is a nonexistent time due to daylight savings time. Try using the 'nonexistent' argument.

pandas@tz2026c.error: ValueError: 2026-03-29 01:30:00 is a nonexistent time due to daylight savings time. Try using the 'nonexistent' argument.

rationale: The widest gap in the tzdb; a correctness test for the gap resolution algorithm rather than for its policy.

title: A monthly recurrence across the Apia date-line jump

normative.title: RFC 5545 erratum 4271 (Verified, Technical, §3.3.10 nonexistent local times)
IANA tz theory.html (zone naming and stability guarantees)

expect.note: Recorded, not scored. 2011-12-30 did not exist in Samoa: the zone jumped from 2011-12-29T23:59:59-10:00 to 2011-12-31T00:00:00+14:00. The 'interpret using the offset before the gap' rule of §3.3.5 yields 2011-12-30T12:00:00-10:00 = 2011-12-30T22:00:00Z, which lands on 2011-12-31T12:00 local — a full calendar day later in local terms.

pandas@tz2026a.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (BYMONTHDAY)

pandas@tz2026c.error: NotImplementedError: pandas: BY* / UNTIL / WKST unsupported (BYMONTHDAY)

rationale: The pathological case for every gap policy: the 'gap' is 24 hours wide and the pre-gap-offset rule produces a wall time on a different date. Any product claiming a DST policy must state what it does here.

title: UTC DTSTART is immune to DST by construction

expect.note: The control for the DST family: a UTC anchor has no gap and no fold, and the local wall time in New York drifts by an hour instead.

rationale: Every hosted scheduler's documented workaround ('use UTC') is this vector. It is correct and it is also the vector that shows what the workaround costs: the wall time moves.

title: Floating DTSTART (no TZID, no Z) has no instants at all

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.5 (DATE-TIME)
normative.quote: Date-time values of this type are said to be 'floating' and are not bound to any time zone in particular. They are used to represent the same hour, minute, and second value regardless of which time zone is currently being observed.

expect.note: Including 2026-03-08T02:30, which is not a valid local time in New York. Floating times are correct here precisely because they are not bound to a zone.

rationale: The third DTSTART value type, and the one that makes the gap/fold question disappear entirely. A model that has no floating type cannot express this vector; a model that has one must decide when the binding to a zone happens.

title: Hourly recurrence across the fold: 25-hour day

normative.title: RFC 5545 §3.3.10 (RECUR value type)
normative.note: FREQ=HOURLY advances by absolute hours, so the repeated wall hour is traversed once in each offset

expect.note: 01:00 appears twice with different offsets. This is the only construct in RFC 5545 that produces two instances with the same wall time, and it is the reason occurrence identity cannot be a wall-clock string.

rationale: Decisive for occurrence identity: any product that keys occurrences by local date-time collapses these two rows and silently drops a run. Paired with CRON-DST-016, which asks the same question of an hourly cron.

title: Hourly recurrence across the gap: 23-hour day

expect.note: 02:00 local never appears; the hours are contiguous in UTC and discontinuous in wall time.

rationale: The gap counterpart of DST-009, and the case where a wall-clock scheduler emits a run that has no instant.

title: Zero-offset transition: Asia/Amman abolishes DST (2022)

normative.title: IANA tz database NEWS
normative.note: Jordan and Syria made +03 permanent in October 2022; the transition changes the abbreviation and the isdst flag but not the offset

expect.note: No wall time is skipped or repeated; an engine that keys gap/fold detection on the isdst flag reports a transition here and mis-resolves the instant.

rationale: The zero-offset transition separates two implementation strategies that are otherwise indistinguishable: comparing utcoffset() (correct) versus comparing dst() or the abbreviation (incorrect).

title: Zero-offset transition: Asia/Damascus abolishes DST (2022)
rationale: Paired with DST-011 so a single zone's data cannot explain a failure.
